title: NeuroListen (Listening to the Brain): sEEG auditory-reconstruction features from 5 participants, authors' per-trial HGA/LFS/BBS arrays
description: Derivative stereo-EEG (sEEG) dataset from five patients with epilepsy who passively listened to spoken Mandarin Chinese words, Mandarin digits and English words (2 s per word). It provides the authors' per-trial high-gamma activity, low-frequency signal and broadband feature arrays at 200 Hz, with bipolar re-referencing and removal of contacts showing epileptiform activity. The data support auditory/speech reconstruction and neural decoding research, and include stimulus audio and mel-spectrograms.
methods_description: sEEG was recorded with Sinovation SDE-10/12/16 depth electrodes (0.8 mm diameter, 3.5 mm contact spacing; 118-186 contacts per participant) on a Nihon Kohden EEG-1200 at 1000 Hz. Stimulus markers sent to a DC channel aligned the audio with the recordings. Contacts with epileptiform activity were removed and the remaining contacts were bipolar re-referenced. High-gamma (70-150 Hz analytic amplitude), low-frequency (low-pass 100 Hz) and combined broadband features were computed at 200 Hz and normalised within each 2 s window.
